% hostile_reads.tex -- the document PR #21 exists to defeat.
%
% Sibling of hostile_write18.tex, and the same idea from the other side: that
% one proves --untrusted refuses \write18, this one proves the sandbox refuses
% \openin. --untrusted does NOT confine reads; measured in PR #19, where
% \openin on /proc/self/environ returned DATABASE_URL, S3_SECRET_KEY,
% API_KEY_SALT and WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET into the PDF a client got back.
%
% HOW TO READ THE RESULT: the page count IS the verdict. Every successful read
% fires a \newpage, so
%
%     1 page  -> every attempt was refused
%     n pages -> n-1 reads succeeded, and the PDF names which
%
% That is deliberate. Reading the typeset TEXT back means decoding a subsetted
% font; counting pages does not, so the test cannot be fooled by an encoding
% nobody checked.
%
% The TeX bundle is deliberately NOT probed here. It is granted read-only by
% design -- the engine cannot typeset without it -- and an earlier version of
% this file probed it, read binary, and aborted before the later attempts,
% reporting four refusals as though they were six.
%
% Measured 2026-09-06 through the live API: status done, 1 page.

\documentclass{article}
\newread\f
\newcommand\probe[1]{%
  \openin\f=#1
  \ifeof\f\else\read\f to \line \newpage READ #1\fi
  \closein\f}
\begin{document}
Base page.
\probe{/etc/hostname}
\probe{/etc/passwd}
\probe{/proc/self/environ}
\probe{/proc/self/cmdline}
\probe{../../../etc/hostname}
\probe{/etc/ssl/certs/../hostname}
\probe{/root/.ssh/id_rsa}
\probe{/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token}
\end{document}
